etymologies.etymologyHTML: From up- +‎ grade.

quote.citation: 1931, Journal of the Outdoor Life‎[1], volume 28, page 303:
quote.text: The Worthens sighed with relief as the engine began its night of upgrade chugging.

definitions.definition: An improved component or replacement item, usually applied to technology.

quote.citation: 2022 January 12, “Network News: Portsmouth line upgrade set to begin”, in RAIL, number 948, page 12:
quote.text: "When we're finished in 2024, this upgrade programme will provide a much-improved railway between London Waterloo and Portsmouth," said NR's Wessex Route Director Mark Killick.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To improve, usually applied to technology, generally by complete replacement of one or more components.
(transitive) To improve the equipment or furnishings of or services rendered to.

quote.citation: 2014, Sid Davis, A Survival Guide for Buying a Home - Page 80‎[2]:
quote.text: From the builder's standpoint, the name of the game is to upgrade you to the maximum you can qualify for.

quote.citation: 2019 October, “South Wales open access bid”, in Modern Railways, page 15:
quote.text: Calls at Cardiff Parkway are proposed once this station opens, with investment promised to upgrade station facilities at Severn Tunnel Junction.

quote.citation: 2022 December 14, “Network News: Fawley branch line reopening supported by 80% of locals”, in RAIL, number 972, page 20:
quote.text: Several level crossings would have to be upgraded, with the existing track re-laid to allow a line speed of 60mph.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To improve in condition or status.
(intransitive, transitive, computing) To replace a program with a later version of itself, a version having a higher version number or marketed under a more recent product name.

quote.text: Men fell out, worn-out, and there were sunstroke cases. It was an eight-mile march upgrade.

quote.citation: 2009, Craig Sanders, Canton Area Railroads‎[4], page 66:
quote.text: Northbound trains originating near the Ohio River faced a 26-mile climb upgrade to Flushing.

quote.citation: 2010, Elliott Merrick, True North: A Journey Into Unexplored Wilderness‎[5], page 167:
quote.text: From there it was an eight-mile pull upgrade to the mountain top.

quote.citation: 2013, Marty Metras, Walking the Walk, Camino de Santiago 2012‎[6], page 16:
quote.text: I did that and saw we had to go upgrade a long ways.

quote.citation: 2020 December 16, David Clough, “Class 37s at 60: the great survivors”, in Rail, page 55, photo caption:
quote.text: [...] 37905 hauls the 1,400-tonne 0730 Mossend-Margam upgrade from Shrewsbury, mainly at 1-in-100, through Church Stretton at around 25mph on May 13 1989.
